findings.title: Prometheus alert rules are not routed anywhere
evidence: infra/digitalocean/prometheus.yml:14-17 — alerting block forwards firing alerts to alertmanager:9093
infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:244-307 — alertmanager v0.28.1 service is defined, internal-only, with healthcheck
infra/digitalocean/alertmanager.tmpl.yml:63-100 — routing tree: critical -> critical receiver, Watchdog -> watchdog receiver, catch-all -> default
.github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:739-747 — prod deploy fails closed when ALERTMANAGER_WATCHDOG_WEBHOOK_URL is empty
findings.impact: The original defect (rules evaluated but alerts visible only in an internal Prometheus UI) is closed: alerts now route to Alertmanager and to the org ntfy instance. Residual risk is verification, not routing: there is no in-repo evidence a synthetic alert actually traversed the path.
findings.recommendation: Keep the routing as-is; close the verification gap by dispatching one synthetic alert (amtool/Prometheus UI) and recording the ntfy delivery as a release artifact.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: prometheus.yml alerting block + alertmanager service + routing tree + prod fail-closed guard all present; ntfy basic-auth receivers added in mainecybertech#154. Residual: docs/RELEASE_GATE.md:34,64 still list 'synthetic alert delivered' as an unchecked exit condition, and promtool/amtool validation is manual only (prometheus.rules.test.yml:3-6).

findings.title: No committed dashboards or SLO/error-budget definitions
evidence: infra/digitalocean/dashboards/mct-overview.json:1-108 — Grafana-importable dashboard with 7 panels (availability, p95 latency, 5xx rate, webhook/notification success, RLS share, active orgs/users)
docs/SLO.md:10-31 — 5 SLOs with PromQL, targets and an error-budget policy (43 min/30d, fast-burn/slow-burn)
docs/SLO.md:32-40 — states the stack ships Prometheus + Alertmanager only; Grafana must be added to render the dashboard
findings.impact: Definitions are committed and reviewed (quarterly cadence stated). Residual: no Grafana service exists, so the dashboard is an importable artifact only, and Prometheus has no published ports (compose:207-237) — operators must SSH-tunnel to use the PromQL.
findings.recommendation: Either add a Grafana service to the compose stack and provision the JSON, or document the SSH-tunnel workflow in MONITORING_AND_ALERTING.md; also add the missing latency/webhook/notification alert rules promised by the SLO table.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: both artifacts exist (dashboard JSON 108 lines, SLO.md 40 lines). Residual: docs/SLO.md:15 promises a latency page at p95>2s/10m and :16-17 list webhook/notification objectives with no alert rule in prometheus.rules.yml — tracked separately in the 'most golden-signal and SLO metrics have no alert rules' finding.

findings.title: Backup/restore is scheduled but not verified on the deployed branch
evidence: .github/workflows/db-backup.yml:14 — job runs in environment 'dev' (backups target the dev database/buckets)
.github/workflows/db-restore-test.yml:14 — restore test also runs in environment 'dev'; weekly cron at line 5

findings.recommendation: Run db-restore-test against a production-derived snapshot (or add a prod-environment restore job with approval), record the green run URL in RELEASE_GATE, and assert row counts/checksums, not just table presence.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: workflows and ntfy notifiers present (mainecybertech#157); prod/deployed-branch restore still not evidenced. Previously recorded partially-fixed at 9c0b88c — unchanged.

findings.title: Total loss of the monitoring/alerting path has no independent dead-man's-switch receiver
evidence: infra/digitalocean/alertmanager.tmpl.yml:86-100,144-152 — Watchdog alert routed to a dedicated watchdog receiver with repeat_interval 5m
infra/digitalocean/alertmanager.tmpl.yml:32-38 — receiver URL is documented as an off-box heartbeat endpoint, not on the droplet
infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:239-307 — alertmanager service, internal only, state volume, healthcheck
.github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:728-747 — production deploy fails when ALERTMANAGER_WATCHDOG_WEBHOOK_URL is empty; dev warns
docs/MONITORING_AND_ALERTING.md:271-352 — operating model incl. 'what happens when the whole stack dies'
findings.impact: The control is implemented end to end in code/config: a dead Prometheus/Alertmanager/droplet stops the heartbeat and the external service pages. Remaining uncertainty is operator-side (whether the secret is set) and exercise evidence.
findings.recommendation: Record one observed heartbeat and one deliberate missed-heartbeat drill (stop alertmanager, confirm the external page) as a release artifact; keep the prod fail-closed guard.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: watchdog route/receiver + prod fail-closed guard present (mainecybertech#154 era). Not exercised: no in-repo artifact shows the external receiver was ever pinged or paged (RELEASE_GATE.md:64-65 unchecked); the URL value is an operator secret and cannot be verified from the repo — marked not exercised rather than unverified-broken.

findings.title: No alerting on audit-trail gaps or privileged (impersonation/admin) abuse
evidence: apps/api/src/lib/metrics.ts:125-130 — portal_impersonation_events_total; services/impersonation.ts:46 increments on every impersonation_log write
infra/digitalocean/prometheus.rules.yml:48-56 — MCTImpersonationBurst alert (>0.5 events/s over 10m)
no metric or rule exists for audit-write failures, missing audit rows, or export/gap detection (grep of prometheus.rules.yml and metrics.ts)
findings.impact: Privileged cross-tenant access now has a runtime alert (the high-value half is fixed). A silent audit-trail gap (writes failing or being skipped) would still go undetected, which undermines the evidence the alert itself relies on.
findings.recommendation: Add a counter for failed/skipped audit writes and an alert on non-zero rate; add a daily reconciliation of expected vs written audit rows where feasible.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: impersonation burst alert present (was added before 9c0b88c); audit-trail gap alerting still absent. Previous register said open — updated to partially-fixed with residual documented.

findings.title: No alerting when webhook dead-letters accumulate or payment reconciliation drifts
evidence: apps/api/src/lib/metrics.ts:136-145 — portal_webhook_dead_letters_total; worker metrics.ts:65-70 — worker_webhook_dead_letters_total
apps/api/src/lib/webhook-dispatcher.ts:124, worker tasks webhook-dispatcher.ts:128, webhook-retry.ts:175,208 — counters incremented

infra/digitalocean/prometheus.rules.yml:1-143 — no rule references any webhook/dead-letter/reconciliation metric
findings.impact: Dead letters and reconciliation drift are exactly the 'silent data-integrity' failures; they are now measurable but nothing alerts, so an operator must query Prometheus manually.
findings.recommendation: Add alert rules on rate(portal_webhook_dead_letters_total)/rate(worker_webhook_dead_letters_total) > 0 and on reconciliation error counts; export a stripe-reconcile metric (reconciled/errors/suspended) and alert on errors>0 or drift>0.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: dead-letter counters exist (added 68fd8d12) but no rule; stripe-reconcile still has no metric. Previous register open — confirmed still open.

.github/workflows/db-backup.yml:59-62 — external ntfy delivery for backup failures (mainecybertech#157)

findings.title: Most golden-signal and SLO metrics have no alert rules (latency, circuit breaker, auth failures, notification/webhook failures, worker jobs, queue depth)
evidence: infra/digitalocean/prometheus.rules.yml:8,18,33,48,94,120 — only six rules exist; a name-by-name comparison shows 4 of 30 declared metric names referenced
docs/SLO.md:15 — promises a latency page at p95>2s/10m; no such rule exists (portal_http_request_duration_seconds unalerted)
apps/api/src/lib/metrics.ts:37-42,86-91,99-118,136-145 — auth failures, circuit-breaker state, notification delivery, webhook dead letters all unalerted
apps/worker/src/metrics.ts:9-29,65-70 — task executions/duration/queue depth and worker dead letters unalerted; task-registry.ts:48-67 emits failure/error statuses
apps/worker/src/health-server.ts:10-31 — a disconnected queue reports status 'degraded' but still HTTP 200, so container health never fails
findings.impact: A stalled queue, failing jobs, an open provider circuit breaker, an auth-failure spike, or notification/webhook delivery failures are invisible to alerting; the first signal may be a user report. The SLO table overstates alert coverage.
findings.recommendation: Add rules: worker_task_executions_total{status=~'failure|error'} rate>0; worker_task_queue_depth > N or queue='unavailable'; portal_circuit_breaker_status==2; portal_auth_attempts_total{result='failure'} spike; notification/webhook failed-rate and dead-letter rate; p95 latency >2s/10m. Add promtool tests for each and run them in CI.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d; covers the OBS half of CHAIN-P2-010 (silent worker failures) and the SLO promises in docs/SLO.md.

findings.title: HTTP metric labels use the raw request path, creating unbounded Prometheus series cardinality
evidence: apps/api/src/middleware/request-id.ts:43 — httpRequestsTotal.inc({ route: req.path, ... })
apps/api/src/middleware/request-id.ts:47 — httpRequestDuration.observe({ route: req.path, ... })
no route-normalization helper exists (grep for req.route/normalizeRoute finds only the OpenAPI extractor)
infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:224,232 — 30d retention with a 256MB Prometheus memory limit
findings.impact: Every URL with an embedded id (/api/v1/tickets/<uuid>, documents, webhooks, etc.) creates new time series per method/status/bucket. Cardinality grows without bound, raising Prometheus memory/disk pressure; a TSDB OOM would take monitoring down (leaving only the external watchdog).
findings.recommendation: Label with the Express route template (req.baseUrl + req.route?.path) or an allow-list of normalized routes; add a unit test asserting ids do not appear as labels.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d.

findings.title: Web error tracking is silently disabled in production (code reads NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN; deploy provides SENTRY_DSN)
evidence: apps/web/sentry.server.config.ts:3, apps/web/sentry.edge.config.ts:3, apps/web/instrumentation-client.ts:3 — all read process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN
infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:190-194 — web service receives SENTRY_DSN (unused by the web Sentry configs)
.github/workflows/build-push.yml:191-196 — web build args do not include NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN
docs/MONITORING_AND_ALERTING.md:162 — claims Sentry is initialized in all 3 services; docs/ADMIN_FEATURES.md:293 documents the NEXT_PUBLIC_ requirement
findings.impact: Browser, server and edge errors from the web app are never reported in production; the documented Sentry alert rules for web issues can never fire. Silent because Sentry.init is skipped when the DSN is falsy.
findings.recommendation: Pass NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN (Sentry DSNs are public by design) into the web image build and/or the web container env; add a boot warning in production when it is missing; update docs.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d.

findings.title: Alerting configuration is not validated in CI and the deploy health gate ignores Prometheus/Alertmanager
evidence: infra/digitalocean/prometheus.rules.test.yml:1-6 — promtool check/test documented as manual docker runs
.github/workflows/validate.yml:1-110 and test.yml — no promtool/amtool step (grep across .github/workflows finds none)
.github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:835-858 — container health gate checks only api, web, worker
infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:207-237 — prometheus has no healthcheck; alertmanager:302-307 has one but is not gated
findings.impact: A syntax/reachability error in prometheus.rules.yml or a broken alertmanager template ships with a green deploy: Prometheus/Alertmanager can fail to start while the workflow reports success, leaving monitoring dead until the external watchdog notices.
findings.recommendation: Add a CI job running promtool check rules + promtool test rules (prometheus.rules.test.yml) and amtool check-config on a rendered template; extend the deploy gate to require prometheus and alertmanager healthy and assert up{job=~'mct-api|mct-worker'}==1 after deploy.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d; the register's 'promtool/amtool checks green' claim referred to manual checks during remediation, not CI.

findings.title: Empty METRICS_TOKEN has no deploy guard and is documented as optional; it breaks the API scrape and fires a false service-down alert
evidence: .github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:722-727 — metrics-token file written from METRICS_TOKEN with chown/chmod but no non-empty check (contrast the watchdog guard at 739-747)
apps/api/src/app.ts:154-164 + routes/health.ts:16-26 — API 404s /metrics unless a token is configured and presented
infra/digitalocean/prometheus.yml:19-32 — mct-api scrape requires the bearer credentials_file
docs/GITHUB_SECRETS_AND_VARIABLES_MATRIX.md:78 and docs/ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES.md:77 — still describe METRICS_TOKEN as optional
commit 8f8dbe42 — the unauthenticated scrape previously made MCTServiceDown fire on a healthy API
findings.impact: If the secret is unset/empty, the scrape 404s, up==0 for 2m, and a critical MCTServiceDown page fires on a healthy API (exactly the incident PR #155 fixed); meanwhile real metrics are absent. Deploy stays green.
findings.recommendation: Fail the prod deploy when METRICS_TOKEN is empty (mirror the watchdog guard), require a non-empty file, update the secrets matrix/env docs to 'required for monitoring', and assert up{job='mct-api'}==1 in the post-deploy health check.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d; builds on mainecybertech#155/#166/#167 which fixed the credential file path/permissions but not the empty-value case.

findings.title: Alert delivery and the dead-man's switch are configured but never exercised end-to-end; no monitoring-of-monitoring rules
evidence: docs/RELEASE_GATE.md:34 — exit condition 'Alertmanager is wired to a receiver and a synthetic alert is delivered'
docs/RELEASE_GATE.md:64-65 — operator checklist item 'synthetic alert delivery' still unchecked
docs/MONITORING_AND_ALERTING.md:320-322 — 'should be tested by stopping alertmanager and confirming the external service reports the missed heartbeat' (no recorded drill)
infra/digitalocean/prometheus.rules.yml:1-143 — no rule on prometheus_rule_evaluation_failures_total or alertmanager notification failures; no exporter/probe freshness metrics
findings.impact: A misconfigured receiver URL, wrong ntfy credentials, or a dead external heartbeat endpoint is invisible until a real incident; the platform cannot currently prove its alerting path works.
findings.recommendation: Dispatch one synthetic alert and record the ntfy delivery; run one missed-heartbeat drill and record the external page; add meta-alerts (rule-evaluation failures, Alertmanager notification failures) and a freshness check on the watchdog heartbeat.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d; the release gate treats this as a pre-go-live exit condition.

findings.title: Container logs are not persisted off-box and are destroyed by the deploy's `compose down`
evidence: infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:19-23 — json-file driver, max-size 10m, max-file 3 (bounded per container)
.github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:809 — `docker compose -p mct-portal down --remove-orphans` removes the previous containers and their logs before `up`
docs/MONITORING_AND_ALERTING.md:49-52 — log forwarding to a central service is listed as 'future'
no `log` directive in infra/digitalocean/Caddyfile or Caddyfile.prod (edge access logs absent)
findings.impact: During an incident the available log window is ~30MB per container and the previous deployment's logs are deleted by the next deploy, so crash-loop or pre-deploy evidence can be lost; there is no cross-service search, and edge (Caddy) requests are not logged at all.
findings.recommendation: Ship logs off-box (DO agent/Loki/vector) or snapshot `docker compose logs` to an artifact before `down`; enable Caddy access logs with rotation; document the retention window in MONITORING_AND_ALERTING.md.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d.

findings.title: API/worker Sentry release markers are not delivered (no SENTRY_RELEASE/GIT_SHA)
evidence: apps/api/src/lib/sentry.ts:11 — release: env.SENTRY_RELEASE ?? process.env.GIT_SHA
apps/worker/src/main.ts:18-19 — same fallback
.github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:647,676 — deploy forwards only SENTRY_DSN; no SENTRY_RELEASE or GIT_SHA
infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:78,141 — api/worker env has SENTRY_DSN only; web bakes NEXT_PUBLIC_GIT_SHA at build (build-push.yml:194)
findings.impact: API/worker errors and performance events are not tagged with the deploy they belong to, so regressions cannot be correlated to a release; web has a marker only in the client bundle.
findings.recommendation: Add SENTRY_RELEASE (or GIT_SHA) to the deploy envs and compose api/worker services; mirror it for web server-side Sentry.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d; INFRA-P2-006 already noted Sentry release/sample rely on defaults.

findings.title: Alertmanager secret provisioning gaps: matrix omits ALERTMANAGER_*; awk renderer breaks on '&' or backslash in values
evidence: infra/digitalocean/alertmanager.tmpl.yml:27-51 — required env names documented only in the template header
docs/GITHUB_SECRETS_AND_VARIABLES_MATRIX.md:1-120 — no ALERTMANAGER_* or NTFY_ALERTS_* rows (grep finds none)
infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:280-292 — rendering uses awk gsub(), where '&' in a replacement expands to the matched text; the guard at :291 then aborts the container
.github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:748-751 — deploy only warns when a critical URL is set without credentials
findings.impact: Operators cannot provision alerting from the secrets matrix; a secret containing '&' or a backslash (plausible in generated passwords/URLs) corrupts the rendered config and Alertmanager exits — which the deploy gate does not detect.
findings.recommendation: Add the ALERTMANAGER_*/NTFY_* rows to the secrets matrix; render with a method that escapes replacement metacharacters (or reject values containing '&' at deploy time with a clear error); gate on alertmanager health.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d; awk replacement semantics are certain, whether any live secret contains such characters is unknown.

findings.title: Metrics rate limiter leaves almost no headroom for the 15s scrape (max 5/min vs 4/min)
evidence: apps/api/src/middleware/rate-limit.ts:68-76 — /metrics limited to 5 requests/min per IP, skipping only 127.0.0.1/::1
infra/digitalocean/prometheus.yml:5 — global scrape_interval 15s (4 scrapes/min from the prometheus container IP)
findings.impact: Any additional /metrics request in the same minute from the scrape IP (manual debug, retry, a second scraper) returns 429 and fails that scrape; repeated 429s can flap up==0 and trigger a false MCTServiceDown.
findings.recommendation: Skip the limiter for authenticated/internal scrapes or raise the limit well above the scrape rate; assert scrape success after deploy.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d.

findings.title: No repository evidence of external uptime checks for platform endpoints; an edge/proxy failure is undetected in-stack
evidence: infra/digitalocean/prometheus.rules.yml:8-16 — MCTServiceDown covers only up{job=~'mct-api|mct-worker'} internal scrapes (containers can be up while the public edge is down)
infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:310-337 — caddy has no monitoring or alert path; its healthcheck only runs `caddy validate`
docs/MONITORING_AND_ALERTING.md:210-211 — CPU/disk 'DO monitoring' claims are not represented anywhere in the repo

no blackbox exporter, uptime check config, or external probe in the repository (grep); the uptime-monitor product module (apps/worker/src/tasks/module-tasks.ts:500-560) monitors tenant-supplied URLs, not the platform
findings.impact: If Caddy crashes, a certificate expires, or DNS/TLS breaks while the API/worker containers stay healthy, users are down but no in-stack alert fires; only deploy-time checks and the alerting-path watchdog exist.
findings.recommendation: Add an external uptime check (DO Uptime, healthchecks-style probe, or blackbox_exporter) for https://api.<domain>/health and the app login page, delivered to the same ntfy topic, and record its configuration in MONITORING_AND_ALERTING.md.

# Observability, Monitoring, and Incident Readiness Audit

## Audit Metadata

- Audit name: `repo-deep-dive` (full hardening rerun)
- Run: `mainecybertech-20261011-0426-full-main-8d299b8`
- Repository: `mainecybertech` (monorepo: api / worker / web, Supabase, single DigitalOcean droplet)
- Branch: `main` @ `8d299b8d` (merge of PR #168)
- Generated at: 2026-10-11
- Auditor: subagent, domain 14 (area code **OBS**)
- Scope limitations: repository-only review. No production/lab access, no secret values, no live Prometheus/Alertmanager/ntfy calls. "Delivered/configured" is distinguished from "exercised"; operator-side secret presence is marked unverifiable.

## Scope

Reviewed: structured logs, request-id correlation, error tracking (Sentry), metrics (API + worker), tracing, health/readiness, client/API/worker errors, job metrics, DB/queue/webhook/notification metrics, uptime checks, alert rules, Alertmanager routing + ntfy delivery, dashboards/SLOs, incident runbooks, audit/security-log signals, release markers, user-impact and data-quality signals.

Not reviewed: tenant-facing uptime-monitor product internals beyond confirming it is not platform self-monitoring; Sentry account configuration (alert rules are UI-side); DigitalOcean monitoring config (not in repo).

Not reproducible in this audit: Sentry project alert rules (UI-side), DigitalOcean monitoring (not in repo), live ntfy delivery, actual secret values.

## Executive Summary

The observability stack is materially better than the previous audit left it. Since `9c0b88c` the team added ntfy delivery with basic auth to Alertmanager (#154), authenticated the Prometheus→API scrape with a deploy-written `metrics-token` file (#155/#166/#167), and wired the remaining declared metrics (#147). The alert path is now: rules → Alertmanager → org ntfy topic, plus an off-box watchdog dead-man's switch with a production fail-closed deploy guard (IR-P0-003). The committed SLO doc and Grafana-importable dashboard exist, and the RLS/tenant-isolation telemetry is real, wired, and unit-tested (IR-P1-006 is actually fixed — the previous register wrongly recorded it open).

The main weaknesses are in breadth and proof rather than the core path: only 6 alert rules exist for 30 declared metrics, so latency, circuit-breaker state, auth-failure spikes, notification/webhook delivery failures, worker job failures and queue depth are measurable but unalerted. Web error tracking is silently disabled in production (`NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN` is never provided while the deploy passes `SENTRY_DSN`). HTTP metric labels use the raw request path, creating unbounded Prometheus series cardinality against a 256MB memory limit. Alerting configs are not validated in CI, and the deploy health gate ignores Prometheus/Alertmanager, so a broken rules file or an empty `METRICS_TOKEN` ships green. Finally, the alert path has never been exercised end-to-end (no synthetic alert/heartbeat evidence; the release gate still lists it as an exit condition), and the incident docs contradict the deployed topology while referencing two files that do not exist.

Priority actions: (1) exercise the alert path and record evidence; (2) add the missing golden-signal rules and wire `promtool` tests into CI; (3) fix the web Sentry DSN and the `route` label cardinality; (4) add a non-empty `METRICS_TOKEN` deploy guard and gate the deploy on monitoring health.

## Detailed Review

### Item: Alert rules and routing (golden signals)

- Missing controls: latency/SLO-burn, circuit-breaker open, auth-failure spike, notification/webhook failure + dead letters, worker failure/queue depth, disk/memory, edge reachability.
